newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello sees more Australia bank competition.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello sees more Australia bank competition.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday there was still room for increased competition in the banking sector.
He said increased competition would help to reduce interest rates for business loans.

"The fact is that business has only had the benefit of the official rate cut, they haven't had the one and three-quarter percent -- the three-quarter percent on the standard variable (home loan rate) that was caused by increased competition," Costello told parliament.
"As a result, there appears to be still room in relation to the banking sector for increased competition and for business to obtain the benefits of that."

The banks had been slow to pass on the most recent easing of monetary policy, especially when compared with their haste to impose higher interest rates when monetary policy had been tightened, Costello said.

"If one looks at the tightenings of monetary policy in August, October and December of 1994, one can see that the tightening in official rates was reflected in the indicator rates generally within 20 days," he said.
He said in comparison, the banks were taking up to 47, and in one case 54, days to pass on recent official interest rate cuts to customers.

"We've made it clear that, as far as the government is concerned, we believe that the benefits of the easing of official rates should be passed on to small business and passed on with all due haste," Costello said.
Earlier on Tuesday, Australian Prime Minister John Howard said he hoped the government's financial industry inquiry would result in more competition among banks.
The inquiry, headed by businessman Stan Wallis, is due to conclude in March, although a draft report is due to be ready this month.
The Reserve Bank of Australia cut its overnight cash rate by half a percentage point in both July and November, responding to lower inflation and moderate wages growth.
